previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, steroid dependence, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for recurrent symptomatic hypotension following an inability to obtain his prescribed rescue dexamethasone due to a pharmacy back order. He presented with dizziness, slurred speech, and chest pain, preceded by a three-day history of diarrhea consistent with an IBD flare. His hypotension was attributed to relative adrenal insufficiency and gastrointestinal fluid losses. He was treated with IV fluids, IV dexamethasone, and oral and IV potassium repletion. His prednisone dose was increased from 10 mg to 20 mg daily, and a new rescue plan with hydrocortisone 100 mg IM via Act-o Vial was established. His potassium normalized, diarrhea improved, and blood pressure stabilized. He was discharged home with medication adjustments, including liquid potassium supplementation and instructions to titrate torsemide based on edema and blood pressure, with follow-up planned in endocrinology and pain clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ hx psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroids and TNF 
inhibitors who presents from home with worsening anasarca in the 
setting of normal cardiac function.
.  
# SOB/Edema: unclear etiology, presumed secondary to his chronic 
steroid use.  In the past, the patient has had massive shifts in 
fluid, sometimes gaining ___ in a week.  He had nuclear 
stress testing in ___ which showed preserved EF, normal LV 
and RV function, and no focal perfusion defects.  Pulmonary 
function testing was done which shows a restrictive pattern 
typical for someone of his body stature.  Has had normal 
UA/renal function (ruling out nephrotic syndrome, no 
proteinuria), LFTs have been normal as has his INR/albumin 
pointing to normal liver synthetic function.  During this 
admission, after his ___ resolved, he was startd on a lasix gtt. 
 He was aggressively diuresed via multiple methods, including a 
lasix drip and lasix boluses; he always put out many liters to 
any intervention.  Ultimately at the time of discharge, he was 
negative 28 liters of fluid (net negative) over approximately 9 
days.  However, his weight only dropped by 6kg.  Nursing I/O 
were accurate, always emptying Os themselves.  The same scale 
(""A"" scale) was used throughout, and was calibrated 
appropriately.  It is unclear how to make up for the extra 22kg 
of weight that should have been lost based upon I/Os.  The 
patient adamantly denied taking in extra fluids that he was not 
recording.  His medication list was reviewed multiple times for 
extra sources of fluid.  He was maintained throughout on a 1.5L 
fluid restriction.  He had regular bowel movements and adhered 
to a normal hospital diet (as far as anyone could tell).  He was 
discharged off of diuretics (stopped torsemide, metolazone, 
eplerenone) as his weight and I/Os clearly did not correlate, 
and it is very unclear as to why.  He has close follow-up with 
Dr. ___ will review his weight gain/loss off of diuretics 
and will reevaluate in clinic.
.
# ___: On admission found to be in ___ with BUN~60 and Cr 2.2 
from baseline ___.  Likely secondary to combination of two 
things.  1) was tapering his dexamethasone with his outpatient 
endocrinologist.  Per the patient, when he tapers too fast he 
gets ___ secondary to hypotension, which was verified from med 
records.  He required a rescue dose of steroid at home ~4d after 
starting a taper.  The day after his rescue dose, he was seen in 
cardiology clinic for IV diuresis; his BP was 118 at that time, 
and his Bun/Cr was ___.  He likely was on the edge from 
periods of hypotension due to his adrenal insufficiency.  2) In 
cardiology clinic, he received 20mg metolazone and 180mg IV 
lasix.  Likely this aggressive diuresis threw him into ___ in 
the setting of possible adrenal insufficiency.  His renal 
failure quickly resolved in 2 days without diuresis, and 
recurred in minor form (Cr max 1.7 while on lasix gtt).  He was 
discharged with a normal Cr.
.
# Hypokalemia: Very difficult to replete in house, especially 
while on diuretics.  Was receiving 120 PO meqs standing daily 
and receiving ~80-160meqs while actively diuresing in addition 
to the 120meq standing.  Endocrine was consulted for the 
hypokalemia, who felt that it was very likely diuretic induced.  
The patient will follow-up with Dr. ___ in 1 week after 
discharge.
.
# Adrenal Insufficiency: maintained good BPs throughout this 
admission after restarting his home 0.875mg dex dose (started 2d 
prior to admission by the patient after a rescue dose).

# Psoriatic arthritis: severe, presenting currently with a 
psoriatic exacerbation now s/p Stelara therapy.  Maintained on 
his dex/imuran.
